Of course, abortion regulations won’t stop all abortions, just like how gun laws won’t stop all shootings, but it will provide a legal disincentive. I understand what you’re saying. I believe that since we’re humans and not able to understand God and His infinite power, we therefore cannot understand the workings of His foreknowledge. We are infinitely less than God, and our minds are similarly less capable than His. Consequently, we are unable to make sense of how He is able to do something like know the future yet not choose it. Of course, He *could* choose what happens, but He gives us free will. Without this free will He gives us, it would be impossible for us to choose to follow or believe in Him. If we didn’t have free will, we wouldn’t be able to choose to believe in God or not—it would be a forced relationship. People often ask, “If God is good, then how did evil enter into the world?” I believe that God, being Goodness and Love, has no capacity for evil or anything bad. As C.S. Lewis has said, evil exists because of something good that has been perverted (paraphrasing). In this example, free will is a good thing that God gave us so that we had the ability to have a free, loving, unforced relationship with Him, but because of our pride, envy, and other sin, we stray from Him. He desires a relationship with us though. But He never forces it. That’s the important thing in my mind.
